title: The Letter of the Cape Route
premise: In 1747, on a windswept cape town where pearl divers and traders coexist uneasily, Astrid Nystrom has spent her life keeping her head down as an indentured clerk to the Halvard Trading Company. When imperial troops requisition the harbor for a war fleet and seize the company's ledgers—records that hold the true names, debts, and deaths of the town's people—Astrid realizes the ledgers are about to be rewritten by victors who never knew these lives existed. Copying the forbidden master ledger by lantern light, she smuggles the truth out aboard a departing ship with the help of Elias, a diver she loves and a man the ledger lists as drowned. The book ends with Astrid testifying before a naval inquiry at the cost of her freedom, her testimony preserved in the official record while she returns to the cape in chains—and free in every way that matters.
about_author: Ines Galloway is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing colonial trading-company records along coastal museum collections. Her novels draw on the marginalia, debt books, and unnamed names she found in those ledgers.

chapters.title: Salt in the Margins
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. She copies shipping entries in the Halvard Company counting house, invisible among clerks, while her father dives for pearls he'll never own. Establishes her belief that history belongs to captains and companies, not to people like her. Emotional beat: quiet resignation mistaken for contentment.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Lives
chapters.summary: Astrid discovers the master ledger's hidden pages: debts erased, divers listed as 'lost' whose bodies were never searched for, including Elias Voss, marked drowned three years ago. She says nothing. Emotional beat: first crack in her belief that staying invisible keeps you safe.

chapters.title: A Man Marked Drowned
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Alive and diving under a false name for a rival buyer, he spots Astrid at the tide pools. Their charged reunion reveals what the ledger did to him and why he let it. Emotional beat: love rekindled alongside guilt over his silence.

chapters.title: Gunpowder in the Harbor
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Imperial warships anchor without warning; an officer requisitions the town, its stores, its boats, and orders all company records surrendered within the week. The comptroller complies too quickly. Emotional beat: dread—the paper world Astrid knows is being confiscated wholesale.

chapters.title: What the Comptroller Burned
chapters.summary: Astrid secretly witnesses the comptroller burning loose correspondence before the army inventory arrives, saving only what profits him. She pockets a half-scorched page naming a drowned diver who was, in fact, worked to death. Emotional beat: complicity turns to resolve.

chapters.title: The Officer Who Reads
chapters.summary: Lieutenant Brandt's POV. A meticulous requisition officer who genuinely believes accurate records serve justice, he begins auditing the ledgers and notices discrepancies. He interviews Astrid as the junior clerk most familiar with the entries. Emotional beat: dangerous respect between two people who both trust paper.

chapters.title: Debt of Breath
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. He organizes divers to slow-work the requisitioned pearl beds, buying time but risking reprisal. Astrid begs him to flee; he refuses to leave the older divers behind. Emotional beat: loyalty pulling against survival, the book's central tension made flesh.

chapters.title: Copying by Lantern Light
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Night after night she copies the master ledger's true pages into a ciphered shorthand her mother taught her, hiding sheets inside mended sails. Each page is a name the victors' historians will never write. Emotional beat: terrified purpose—she has become a historian herself.

chapters.title: The Informer
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converge. A fellow clerk, jealous and frightened, suspects Astrid's late hours and hints at it to Brandt. Meanwhile the comptroller offers the army a 'corrected' ledger already purged of the company's crimes. Emotional beat: the walls closing in from two directions.

chapters.title: Storm Over the Cape
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. A gale wrecks two warships; the town is blamed for poor pilotage, and Brandt threatens collective punishment unless someone explains the harbor charts. The truth: the company sold the navy outdated charts to hide smuggling routes. Emotional beat: the moment silence becomes betrayal.

chapters.title: Charts and Confessions
chapters.summary: Brandt's POV. Astrid brings him the chart evidence, testing whether his faith in accurate records outweighs his duty to the fleet. He believes her—but warns that what he does with truth depends on whose signature authorizes it. Emotional beat: hope entangled with disillusionment.

chapters.title: The Price of the Pearl Beds
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Reprisals come anyway: a diver is flogged, and Elias learns the army plans to press the divers into salvage labor for the wrecked ships—a death sentence in those waters. Emotional beat: rage crystallizing into decision; they must get the record out now.

chapters.title: A Ship Called Patience
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. A neutral merchant vessel, the Patience, will sail on the spring tide. Astrid and Elias plan to smuggle her copied ledger aboard, but the harbor is sealed and every crate is searched. Emotional beat: claustrophobic urgency.

chapters.title: The Clerk's Mistake
chapters.summary: The informer clerk searches Astrid's quarters and finds one unciphered sheet. Brandt confronts her privately—not with arrest, but with a choice: hand over everything and be protected, or be tried as a spy. Emotional beat: the trap of trusting institutions with your truth.

chapters.title: What Astrid Refused
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. She gives Brandt a partial truth—the chart evidence—to save the town, but hides the ledger of names, knowing once it enters official hands it can be sealed or altered forever. Emotional beat: the painful discovery that even honest men serve systems that erase.

chapters.title: Night Tide
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. The divers stage a coordinated 'accident'—a false distress signal that draws the patrol boat away while Astrid rows the hidden ledger through black water to the Patience. Emotional beat: communal courage; the whole town becomes her accomplice.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: Brandt's POV. Acting on the informer's tip, Brandt boards the Patience at dawn. He finds the ciphered pages—and recognizes Astrid's shorthand from her clerk work. Alone in the cabin, he must decide what to report. Emotional beat: the climax of his character arc, mercy versus career.

chapters.title: The Inquiry
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Brandt reports the ledger 'destroyed by seawater' but summons a formal inquiry into the company's records, requiring sworn testimony. Astrid testifies publicly to the drowned divers, the debts, the burned pages—putting the truth on the record ahead of any victor's historian. Emotional beat: triumphant terror; her voice shaking and unstoppable.

chapters.title: Reckoning of Accounts
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The inquiry indicts the comptroller; the company's charter is suspended pending investigation. But the fleet needs the harbor, so punishments are softened, deals struck. Elias is pardoned as a material witness. Emotional beat: victory that tastes incomplete—history recorded, justice diluted.

chapters.title: Chains and Free Hands
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. For destroying 'company property' (the original pages she copied over), Astrid is sentenced to a term of indentured labor—transferred, ironically, to the naval archive where the inquiry's records are kept. Emotional beat: bitter irony transformed into quiet triumph; she will guard the very record she made.

chapters.title: The Historian's Visit
chapters.summary: Brandt's POV. Years later pattern compressed into weeks: a fleet historian arrives to write the official account and finds Astrid's testimony cited throughout, impossible to excise because it is sworn, signed, and cross-referenced. Brandt, promoted, chooses not to mention how it got there. Emotional beat: vindication—the record held.

chapters.title: Names on the Page
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, final chapter. Serving out her sentence in the archive, she enters new records in her own hand and adds, in the margin beside each lost diver, the name the old ledger denied them. Elias waits at the tide pools when her term ends. Emotional beat: resolution—she was never meant to be invisible; neither were they.
